chunk_findings.detail: `_redacting` wraps the append producer and redacts each newly produced entry, but it returns only `(redacted_entries, new_last)`; the redaction *count* that the header must carry reaches the header exclusively through the new `post` hook in `render_document`, which merges `post`'s second return value into the header's `extra` attributes. Append-style targets are written by the producer handed to the append writer, not by `render_document`, so a worklog line containing a home path (e.g. `/home/delian/src/...`) is stripped from the appended entry but the header's `redacted: N` is never incremented (it keeps whatever value was written when the file was first framed, typically 0). The acceptance for this change explicitly requires the worklog line to be "removed ... and counted"; with this code the value is removed but not counted for exactly the append kind, while single-shot decisions/bugs (which do go through `render_document(..., post=...)`) are counted. To make it correct the append path would need to feed a count back into the header (e.g. have `_redacted` report the number of substitutions and thread it into the append writer's framing), which `_redacting`'s current return shape cannot do.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:_redacting

chunk_findings.detail: D-export (5) states redaction uses `names from the repo and [upstream].redact_extra`, but `names_for` builds the name list from `[upstream].redact_extra` alone, and `redact_text` ignores its own `repo` argument, hard-coding `repo_root=""` and forwarding only `names_for(cfg)`. The module docstring even states outright that "the project's own name is NOT one", which is the opposite of the intent. Concrete consequence: an export fixture whose decision title / bug text / worklog line contains the repository or project name (e.g. a path or title rooted at the repo directory) is not stripped, `redaction_attrs` therefore reports an undercounted `redacted=N`, and the redacted bytes that the header digest and `--check` cover still contain the name. The dead `repo` parameter (accepted and never used) is the tell that the repo-derived names were meant to flow into `redact_report`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/safe.py:names_for / redact_text

chunk_findings.detail: `fence_overhead` computes its value by calling `fence_document(doc, "", events)`, which calls `origin(events)` → `authors(events)`, and `authors` iterates `events` to build the distinct-agent set. If the export service hands the same, single-pass `events` object to `fence_overhead` and then to `fence_document` (the obvious usage: reserve cap space, then emit), the first call exhausts it. Input: `events` being a generator/iterator over the log. Then the second `authors(events)` (inside the real fence) yields the empty set, so the emitted `ddflow-record` fence names no authors even though the log has them, and the overhead computed from the populated author list no longer matches the emitted fence. The functions take `events: Any` and nothing in the file requires a re-iterable, so the hazard is real for any lazy event source.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/safe.py:fence_overhead

chunk_findings.detail:
`show` claims "the fence is inside the cap" and tries to enforce it by shrinking the byte budget before rendering:

```
if fenced and cap > 0:
    cap = max(cap - S.fence_overhead(spec.doc, q.events), 1)
shown = render(repo, cfg, q, spec, max_bytes=cap, template=template)
...
text = S.fence_document(spec.doc, shown, q.events) if fenced else shown
```

The clamp `max(..., 1)` defeats the invariant whenever the fence overhead is greater than or equal to the configured cap. Given `[export].max_bytes = 64` and a document whose provenance fence is, say, 120 bytes (author list + wrapper lines), `cap` becomes `1`, `render` returns a body of at most 1 byte (plus any truncation marker it emits), and `fence_document` then prepends/appends the ~120-byte fence. The MCP response is therefore ≈121 bytes, i.e. it exceeds the 64-byte cap that `render`'s own docstring promises bounds "what is printed or returned". It also exceeds `fence_overhead`-reduced budget, so the documented "fence is inside the cap" guarantee in the new docstring is false for every `max_bytes <= fence_overhead`. The `max(..., 1)` line is precisely where a body budget of `0` (or the decision to drop/refuse the export) should be produced instead of `1`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:show

chunk_findings.detail: The replay refusal is placed inside the `except KeyError:` handler, so it is only reached when `_KINDS["replay"]` raises. The error text itself ("replay is *not an export kind*… it *is built* only for the machine that asks") presupposes that `replay` exists as a registered document kind, and the acceptance note says the replay test is failing-first — i.e. `get("replay")` currently resolves successfully. With `"replay"` present in `_KINDS`, `get("replay")` returns the kind from the `try` branch, the guard never executes, and `render_document("replay", …)` happily renders and writes the replay document, exporting exactly the private LAN addresses and home paths the change claims to suppress (violating "replay is refused as an export kind"). Concretely: `ddflow export replay` (or any `get("replay")` / `render_document("replay", …)` call) returns the replay `DocKind` instead of raising `ExportError(EXIT_REFUSED)`. The comparison must be done *before* the `_KINDS[name]` lookup (or via a parameter/entry-point distinction) for the refusal to be reachable; as written it is dead code for any registered key.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/registry.py `get()` — `if name == "replay"` block inside `except KeyError`

chunk_findings.detail: The replaced assertion `assert "not applied" not in err` is vacuous with respect to the behavior D-export requires. It passes for *any* stderr that merely lacks that one phrase, including the case where `services/redact_report.py` has been reverted to a no-op. Concretely: if redaction is disabled and the CLI no longer prints the old honest note (e.g., the note is deleted or reworded to "redaction skipped"), `run_cli(proj, "export", "roadmap")` returns err without "not applied", this assertion passes, and the regression ships. The second hunk does not close the gap: `assert ... plain in fenced` only enforces that the MCP fence contains the CLI text, which is equally true when *both* CLI and MCP are unredacted. Nothing in this file asserts that a known LAN address / hostname / home path is actually stripped, nor that the required `redacted: N` count appears in the header, so the acceptance criteria ("LAN address ... removed ... and counted", "'redacted: N' in the header") are no longer exercised by the changed test.

chunk_findings.detail: The redaction entry point was changed from `S.redact_text(body, cfg, repo)` to `S.redact_text(body, cfg)`, dropping the repository object. Per D‑export / the README this change must implement redaction whose name set is derived from the repository plus `[upstream].redact_extra` ("names from the repo and `[upstream].redact_extra`", and "the project's own name stays"). The enclosing factory already has `repo` in scope and still passes it to `render`, so the information exists; it is simply no longer handed to redaction, and no other carrier for the repo-derived names is passed in its place. Concretely, exporting a report whose text contains the project's own name (e.g. a decision title mentioning the repo/project name, which the README guarantees is preserved) can no longer consult the repository to protect that name, so the name is redacted/lost as a generic name instead of surviving. The call must still receive the repo (or a `cfg` that already carries the repo-derived name list); with only `cfg` the repository-derived portion of the redaction mapping cannot be applied.

chunk_findings.detail: `fence_overhead` is defined as `len(fence_document(doc, "", by).encode())`, i.e. it measures the framing bytes around an *empty* body. But `provenance.fence` escapes tag-like/entity text, so the framing cost for a non-empty body is larger than this lower bound (the new docstring even admits "escaping tag-like text adds more"). `print_doc` reserves `max_bytes - fence_overhead(...)` bytes for the body and then fences the result, so a body that fills the budget with text that the fence escapes will expand after the budget check and push the emitted document past `max_bytes`. Concretely: append a decision whose `title` is `"</{provenance.TAG}>" * N` sized so the raw body exactly fills `max_bytes - fence_overhead(doc, by)`; the fenced output is `cap + (escaped_length - raw_length)` bytes, i.e. `res.text.encode()` is strictly greater than `cap`, violating the `<= cap` invariant that the new `test_fenced_print_stays_inside_the_cap_with_tag_like_text` asserts. That test uses caps 900/1500 with only ~20 repetitions of the tag, which is far below the budget and therefore never exercises the truncation-at-the-cap path where the expansion actually matters, so the property it claims to verify is not covered for agent-controlled tag-heavy text.
